Balestier Regency relaunched for collective sale at unchanged price of $255 mil
article:
Balestier Regency , a freehold 10-storey apartment at 4 Jalan Ampas, has been relaunched for collective sale by public tender with a guide price of $255 million.

The price is unchanged from when the 72-unit development last launched for tender in May.

“Given the limited availability of sizeable freehold redevelopment sites in the city-fringe market, we believe Balestier Regency remains a relevant acquisition opportunity for developers taking a medium- to long-term view of the market,” commented Low Choon Sin, managing partner of SRI Capital Market in an Oct 13 release. SRI is handling the sale of the site.

The price reflects a land rate of approximately $1,473 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr), including a land betterment charge (LBC) of about $381,181 (based on September 2026 rates).

If the LBC and bonus gross floor area (GFA) for balconies are factored in, the land rate works out to $1,437 psf ppr.

Completed in 1990, Balestier Regency occupies a 61,931 sq ft residential site with a gross plot ratio of 2.8. This translates to a maximum GFA of approximately 173,407 sq ft.

As the development enjoys a high baseline of 2.793, only a nominal LBC is payable, according to SRI. The site can potentially be redeveloped into a new project with up to 161 apartments.

The tender will close at 3pm on Nov 12.

title: Binjai Park shop with 999-year leasehold tenure on the market for $4.4 mil
article:
A strata-titled commercial unit in Binjai Park has been launched for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise at a guide price of $4.4 million.

The ground-floor unit has a 999-year leasehold tenure and spans a strata area of around 1,388 sq ft, which means the price works out to $3,170 psf. The unit is part of a three-storey walk-up shophouse that includes residential units on the upper floors.

The walk-up sits along a row of similar shophouses in the Binjai Park residential enclave in Bukit Timah. It is within walking distance of the King Albert Park MRT Station on the Downtown Line.

Looking to invest in overseas properties ? Explore projects available for sale around the world

The unit up for sale is currently tenanted, according to Huttons Asia, which is handling the sale.

Yeo Khee Liang, associate senior marketing director at the firm, says that commercial units in the Binjai Park estate are rare. “Only around 16 such units are available within the area.”

As a result, he anticipates the property to appeal to a diverse range of buyers. “We expect strong interest from investors and family offices, as well as owner-occupiers such as boutique operators and wellness or education businesses looking for a foothold in this enclave.”

Based on caveats lodged, the last commercial unit to change hands along Binjai Park was a 1,335 sq ft, strata-titled shop that fetched $3.85 million, or $2,884 psf, in November 2024.

Lee Sze Teck, Huttons’ senior director of data analytics, notes that the shophouse segment “continues to attract wealth, underpinned by favourable interest rates, constrained supply and foreign ownership regulations elsewhere in the property market”.

He expects shophouse valuations to be “well-supported over the long term”.

The EOI exercise will close at 3pm on Nov 2.

title: Late tycoon Chng Gim Huat's Lornie Road bungalow back on market at $83 mil
article:
The sprawling freehold bungalow at 8 Lornie Road, formerly the home of the late property tycoon Chng Gim Huat, is back on the market with a guide price of $83 million, or $1,605 psf.

The 51,700 sq ft estate in prime District 11 is being offered for sale by public tender, with Knight Frank Singapore appointed as the exclusive marketing agent.

The property was first launched for sale by private treaty in May 2025 at $82 million, or $1,586 psf. The Chng family subsequently withdrew it from the market. The latest asking price is up $1 million, or 1.2%.

The relaunch follows the family's June sale of the 272-room Orchid Hotel at 1 Tras Link in Tanjong Pagar for about $273 million. Developed by Chng's CGH Group, the hotel opened in 2011.

The buyer of Orchid Hotel was reportedly a joint venture majority-controlled by an entity linked to Leow Ban Leong, one of the two owners of Singapore-based construction and property group Master Contract Services. North America-based Westmont Hospitality Group holds a minority stake in the joint venture. Knight Frank also brokered the hotel sale.

Family home dating back to 1937

The pre-war bungalow at 8 Lornie Road dates back to 1937 and is believed to have been purchased by Chng in the 1970s from the late Kwek Hong Png, founder of Hong Leong Group and father of City Developments Ltd (CDL) executive chairman Kwek Leng Beng.

Chng, who died in August 2024 at 90, lived in the house with his wife and seven children — five sons and two daughters.

Over the decades, the house was expanded to accommodate the growing family. In the 1990s, the family added two bedrooms to the second floor and built an office suite for the family's investment holding company, Chng Gim Huat Holdings, on the ground floor.

The estate also has an expansive garden with mature fruit trees, including durian, mango, avocado, longan, pomelo and starfruit.

In a May 2025 interview with EdgeProp Singapore, Chng's son Alex recalled how the family would gather in his father's office after dinner to discuss business.

Chng also acquired an adjoining bungalow plot in 1987 and redeveloped it into two pairs of semi-detached houses -- one for four of his four sons.

Redevelopment potential

According to Knight Frank, the 8 Lornie Road site has about 58m of road frontage and offers redevelopment potential.

When the property was first marketed in 2025, Knight Frank indicated that the site could be subdivided into six detached houses or 16 semi-detached houses, subject to approval by the relevant authorities.

Alternatively, the site could be retained as a single private estate for a multigenerational family.

"Beyond its immediate redevelopment potential, 8 Lornie Road offers the opportunity to secure a substantial freehold estate in a market where opportunities of this nature are increasingly difficult to replicate," says Dayna Ang, senior manager of capital markets at Knight Frank Singapore.

Alternatively, the site could be retained as a single private estate for a multigenerational family.

Ang considers the guide price of $1,605 psf on land "an attractive entry point" for buyers with a long-term investment horizon.

Melvin Chay, interim head of capital markets at Knight Frank Singapore, says the firm continues to see interest from developers and private investors in well-located freehold residential assets.

"While developers are focused on development feasibility and end-buyer demand, private buyers tend to place greater emphasis on location, privacy and long-term ownership," he says.

The tender for 8 Lornie Road will close on Nov 12 at 3pm.

title: GEO ENERGY: Road Is Open — And Payoff Has Begun. Will Share Price Follow?
article:
Geo Energy has built the road. Now comes the exciting part — putting it to work and reaping the rewards.

Its 92-km coal-hauling road and associated jetty,
developed under PT Marga Bara Jaya (MBJ),
have been operational since July 2026.
The infrastructure primarily serves the Triaryani (TRA) mine which is majority-owned by Geo.

developed under PT Marga Bara Jaya (MBJ),

And management is thinking big.

In a 9 Oct investor webinar organised by Phillip Securities,
Chief Operating Officer Philip Hendry and CFO Adam Tan
offered a more detailed roadmap for the next two years.

Chief Operating Officer Philip Hendry and CFO Adam Tan

For 2027, Geo is targeting
17–19 million tonnes
of group coal production in 2027 (2026 target: 11.5–12.5 million tonnes).

Strikingly, management anticipates
another roughly 50% y-o-y
increase in coal volumes in 2028.

It is an ambition, not guaranteed output.

If achieved, Geo could be looking at a very different scale of operations in just two years.

Bigger trucks, then a bigger jetty

The operational details are becoming more concrete.

• Geo said about 250 smaller trucks, carrying 35–45 tonnes each, are already deployed on MBJ.
•
Double-trailer trucks carrying
140 tonnes
started being deployed in October.
•
Management aims to have about
67 double trailers by Dec 2026
and
100 by 1H2027
.

•

•

These numbers give investors a concrete idea of the ramp-up.

There is another important distinction: the road’s capacity is not the same as the entire infrastructure’s capacity.

The Phase 1 jetty, from which coal is loaded onto barges for onward shipment, currently limits throughput to
20–25 million tonnes annually
.
Management intends to begin developing Phase 2 during 2027, with construction taking nine to 12 months and operations targeted for
early 2028
.
That would enable approximately 50 million tonnes of annual infrastructure capacity.

Choosing the right customers

MBJ’s attraction extends beyond transporting Geo’s own TRA coal. Nearby miners could become paying road users.

Geo says it has secured binding term sheets covering nine million tonnes of annual third-party haulage.
Management is nevertheless still evaluating prospective customers and negotiating commercial arrangements, including with those counterparties.

Management used the analogy of a landlord choosing reliable tenants: the objective is not simply to fill space, but to select customers capable of paying through coal-market fluctuations.
Third-party usage is expected sometime in 2027. However, no firm revenue figure or start date was supplied.

MBJ has the potential to generate up to US$250 million in annual third-party EBITDA at full capacity (25 million tonnes external capacity), alongside logistics savings on Geo’s own coal.

Tonnes of savings

Management also explained the expected savings of more than US$10 per tonne routed through MBJ.

Avoiding external tolls saves US$7–8 per tonne, while more efficient haulage contributes another US$6–7, partly offset by MBJ’s operating and maintenance costs.
Importantly, the benefit is already showing up in its operating costs.
Geo reported achieving ~US$11/tonne of cash cost reduction on tonnage through MBJ in 3Q2026.
Group coal sales totalled about
3.3 million tonnes
in 3Q2026, almost matching the 3.6 million tonnes sold in the entire first half.

Importantly, the benefit is already showing up in its operating costs.

Will stronger earnings convince the market?

Geo's stock price has been volatile, though it's +28% year-to-date.  The stock has retreated from its end-Sept level of 62 cents, suggesting that investors are cautious given the market-wide sluggishness.

With coal prices strengthening and production ramping up, Geo should report substantially stronger earnings for 3Q and 4Q2026. That could catalyse a re-rating of the stock.
The benchmark ICI4 coal price now sits ~31% above its 1H2026 average, and forward pricing points to ~US$78/t through the end of 2027.
Management attributed stronger coal prices to rising electricity demand, including from AI and data centres, alongside energy-security concerns arising from the Middle East conflict.
CFO Adam Tan said more expensive gas was also encouraging power producers to reactivate older coal-fired plants.
On 28 Sept, Geo said it expected sales volume and net profit for 3Q2026 to increase significantly against not just 3Q2025, but also each of the first two quarters of 2026.

Truck deployment, third-party contracts, the ResInvest agreement and 2027-2028 mining ambitions add up to a significant potential boom in Geo Energy's future.

title: Beyond STI: 3 SGX Stocks Quietly Buying Back Their Own Shares
article:
Singapore companies are
buying back
their own shares at a record pace.
In the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), 80 primary-listed companies bought back S$2.38 billion of their own shares on the open market.
That already tops 2025’s full-year total of S$2.23 billion, which was itself a 10-year high on the SGX.
Singapore Telecommunications Ltd
(SGX: Z74), or Singtel,
Keppel Ltd
(SGX: BN4), and
United Overseas Bank Ltd
(SGX: U11), or UOB, led the charge, spending S$1.72 billion between them – or 72% of the total.
Further down the list, three dividend payers outside the
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI) are buying too.
Together, they spent S$1.87 million, less than 0.1% of the market total.

These are small sums, so why look?
A buyback means more when you read it next to the
dividend
and the cash that pays for both.
Can Micro-Mechanics fund its growth plan and its dividend?
Micro-Mechanics
(SGX: 5DD) makes precision consumable tools and parts for semiconductor processing.
For the financial year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2026), revenue grew 15.8% year on year (YoY) to S$75.5 million.
Consumable tools, which represent 80% of sales, grew 19.8% to S$60.4 million.
Gross margin widened to 51.6% from 49.4%, while net profit attributable to owners climbed 28.3% to S$15.9 million.
The cash side held steady.
Free cash flow came in at S$16.8 million, broadly flat compared with the previous year.
As at 30 June 2026, Micro-Mechanics had S$30.1 million in cash reserves and no bank borrowings.
The total dividend held at S$0.06 per share.
The buyback barely dents that cash.
Micro-Mechanics bought back 250,000 shares for S$738,521 in 9M2026, all before September.
That is about 4.4% of FY2026 free cash flow.
The bigger call on cash lies ahead.
Management aims to lift revenue to at least S$150 million within five years, roughly double FY2026 level.
Capital expenditure is set to rise to S$12 million in FY2027.
China contributed 34.2% of total revenue, and management highlighted geopolitical uncertainty as a key risk factor to monitor.

Can Nordic turn a record order book into cash?
Nordic Group
(SGX: MR7) is an engineering services provider to the semiconductor, defence, petrochemical and marine sectors.
In the first half of 2026 (1H2026), revenue rose 3% YoY to S$87.2 million.
Profit grew much faster.
Net profit attributable to shareholders climbed 21% to S$10 million, partly because lower borrowings cut finance costs by 51%.
Cash flow tells a softer story.
Free cash flow fell 28% YoY to S$10.2 million as working capital absorbed cash and tax and capital expenditure payments rose.
Operating cash flow before working capital changes nevertheless improved to S$14.9 million.
The balance sheet got stronger anyway.
Net cash expanded to S$10.2 million as of 30 June 2026, up from S$4.1 million at the end of 2025.
The board raised the interim dividend to S$0.010 per share from S$0.008, which was paid out on 4 September 2026.
Nordic has not stopped buying either.
It repurchased 1,125,700 shares for S$625,731 in 9M2026, and about 37% of that came in September.
Looking forward, the pipeline appears full.
Its order book hit a record S$254.3 million as at 30 June 2026, mostly for delivery over the next 36 months.
The next step is turning that work into free cash flow.

What happens to Boustead’s dividend once the one-off gain fades?
Boustead
Singapore
(SGX: F9D) is an engineering and technology group.
For the financial year ended 31 March 2026 (FY2026), revenue rose 18% YoY to S$624.4 million.
The headline profit figure needs a closer look.
Net profit rose 145% year on year to S$232.6 million, largely driven by a S$140.8 million gain from selling assets to UI Boustead REIT (SGX: UIBU).
Strip out exceptional items and net profit would have fallen 35% YoY.
Gross margin also narrowed to 35% from 44%.
Boustead’s dividends follow the same split.
Ordinary dividends comprised an interim dividend of S$0.015 per share and a proposed final dividend of S$0.04.
The board also proposed a special dividend of S$0.045, bringing total distributions to S$0.10 per share, compared with S$0.075 a year earlier.
Cash flow went the other way.
Free cash flow swung to a negative S$84 million from a positive S$69.7 million in the prior year, as working capital absorbed S$140.7 million due to project execution timing.
Nevertheless, Boustead maintained a healthy net cash position of S$294.6 million as of 31 March 2026, and its September buyback utilised less than 0.2% of that buffer.
The order book offers some comfort.
As of May 2026, the engineering backlog stood at around S$840 million, including S$461 million in contracts secured since the start of FY2027.
Management expects satisfactory results for FY2027.

Get Smart: Start with the cash behind the buyback
Buyback league tables will always favour the large
blue chips
.
For a small cap, measure the buyback against the cash that pays for it.
Free cash flow is the core driver of sustainable dividends, so that is where you start.
Ask whether it covers the ordinary dividend before you credit any buyback or special payout.
A buyback funded from surplus cash adds to your return.
One funded while free cash flow shrinks deserves a harder look.
When they next report, ask one question: Can free cash flow cover the ordinary dividend without help from a one-off gain?

The aim is to make
blue-chip stocks
easier for small investors to buy, and more small investors should mean more trading.
So, has trading volume risen?
What Changed with SGX’s Board Lot Size Reduction?
Before 5 October, all 11 stocks traded in lots of 100 shares, the standard since January 2015, when SGX cut it from 1,000.
Under the new rules, stocks priced between S$10 and S$100 can trade in lots of 10 shares, and those above S$100 in single shares.
So far, only the
first 11 qualifying stocks
have switched.
Together, the 11 stocks made up roughly 35% of SGX trading activity in the first half of 2026.
Only the minimum order size changes, so the share prices, dividends per share and valuations stay untouched.
A stock that moves to a smaller lot keeps it even if its price later falls, and the Singapore Exchange (SGX) will review more stocks every quarter from January 2027, using July to December closing prices.
For stocks priced above S$10, buying in lots of 10 instead of 100 cuts the cost of entry by 90%.
SGX expects the change to lower barriers to participation and improve affordability for retail investors.
More participation could, in turn, support liquidity.
Did Trading Volume Actually Increase?
The banks make a poor test case.
On 7 October 2026, OCBC fell 5.9% after Citi downgraded it to sell, and DBS and UOB also closed lower.
Moves like that lift volumes on their own, so the analysis looks at five eligible names less affected by the bank sell-off: SGX, Keppel, Jardine Cycle & Carriage, Haw Par Corporation and Venture Corporation.
We compare two periods: the 20 trading days from 7 September to 2 October, before the change, and the five sessions from 5 to 9 October, after it.
We look at two measures: average daily volume (ADV), which is the number of shares traded each day, and average daily value, which is the number of shares traded multiplied by the closing price.

Jardine Cycle & Carriage appears to have benefitted the most, suggesting the highest-priced stock benefitted disproportionately.
However, we don’t see this effect flow to SGX and Venture Corporation, both priced higher than Keppel.
Four of the five stocks saw a higher average daily value.
That said, we caution that there are nuances to the data: too few trading sessions have passed and short-term trading volumes may be driven by market sentiment, individual company announcements or general trading conditions.
Why Smaller Board Lots Could Encourage More Trading
The most obvious draw is the lower upfront cost.
Previously, one lot of DBS shares cost roughly S$7,300; now, you can buy shares of the bank with just about S$730.
That also makes it easier to spread money around.
About S$900 now buys 10 shares each of SGX, Keppel, Jardine Cycle & Carriage, Haw Par Corporation and Venture Corporation.
Previously, such a basket would have cost roughly 10 times as much.
Regular investing gets easier too.
Before, an investor who set aside S$500 a month would take about 15 months to buy one board lot of DBS shares; now, it takes just two months.
The Catch: Brokerage Fees Still Matter
Many brokers charge a minimum commission per trade, and a small order feels it most.
A hypothetical S$27 minimum fee on a S$730 purchase (10 DBS shares) works out to 3.7% of the amount, compared with just 0.37% on S$7,300.
Over a round trip, the share price must climb about 7.4% just to break even for the former and roughly 0.74% for the latter.
What you pay depends on the type of
brokerage account
.
Traditional brokers have usually charged a percentage commission with a minimum fee of roughly S$8 to S$27, though some have started reducing minimums on small trades since the change.
Lower-cost trading platforms charge far less, typically a small percentage with a minimum of a few dollars, or none at all.
A lower entry price only helps if commissions stay small relative to the amount invested.
Anyone who buys 10 shares at a time also pays that commission on every purchase.
What Should Investors Watch Next?
It’s too early to tell whether the pickup in trading will last.
The real test is whether volumes stay above their pre-change pace moving forward.
The next few months of trading data should reveal plenty.
Total volume is only part of the picture.
Large institutional orders can swamp it, so the share of trades below 100 shares, the number of trades and the median trade size are better gauges of small-investor participation.
A lower entry price also changes nothing about what the underlying company earns; share prices will still follow earnings and dividends.
Get Smart: Accessibility Is Only the First Step
Smaller lots put the market’s priciest stocks within reach of small investors.
The early trading data is encouraging but far from conclusive.
Four of the five stocks recorded higher average daily volume than before the change.
Jardine Cycle & Carriage posted the biggest jump.
At about S$25, it is the highest-priced of the five, but company news may also have played a part: it is selling its Cycle & Carriage motor businesses, is changing its name and has proposed a special dividend.
If a high share price alone drove trading, SGX and Venture, both priced above Keppel, should have gained more than Keppel did, but they didn’t.
Transaction costs matter, too, so check your broker’s fee schedule and avoid trading just because it’s cheap to start.
The real test is whether liquidity and participation hold up over several months, not one busy week.

title: Trump’s diesel deal irks allies and is unlikely to reduce prices
article:
(Oct 13): US President Donald Trump’s deal for Russian diesel exposed the US to legal questions, opened a rift with his Republican allies and European leaders and heightened tensions with Ukraine — all in exchange for an outcome that experts suggest is unlikely to succeed.

Under the agreement — announced late last week — Russian President Vladimir Putin would begin releasing diesel supplies into global markets as part of a US effort to bring down prices from their record highs before the Nov 3 midterm elections. Trump has also intensified demands on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop attacking Russian refineries and announced an energy ceasefire between the two sides.

The decisions and the ceasefire are all a bet that lowering fuel prices will be the best way to win more votes next month despite the risk of a backlash from political friends and foes alike. On Sunday, a bipartisan group of senators argued that Trump should “reverse course” on his plan to cut a diesel deal with Russia.

“The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians,” the senators said in a statement.

The accord also provoked fresh tension with Europe, where officials warned that it would bolster Moscow’s war effort in Ukraine. They said the US should impose more sanctions instead.

“We would call on the US to put the sanctions in place so that actually we could finish this war, so that all the effects of these attacks on refineries would not be there,” top European Union diplomat Kaja Kallas told reporters in Luxembourg on Monday before meeting with the bloc’s foreign ministers.

See also: Trump lifts sanctions, says Russia to supply diesel to US, world

There’s also the legal challenge. A 2022 law prohibits the US from buying most Russian energy products. It’s still not clear how Trump plans to get around that, and some lawmakers, including Senator Roger Wicker, a Mississippi Republican, have already said they don’t expect the deal to go through.

Trump acknowledged on Monday that neither side had actually committed to stop attacking each other’s energy infrastructure.

“They agreed. You know why? Because I said you agree,” Trump told reporters. “That’s why they agreed — because I said they agreed.”

See also: Australia says doesn’t need Russian fuel after Trump diesel move

“I think actually Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelenskyy,” Trump said.

Keith Kellogg, the president’s former envoy to Kyiv, dismissed Trump’s latest disagreement with Zelenskyy as “noise.” He said he didn’t expect it to escalate to anything similar to their infamous face-to-face argument in the Oval Office in February 2025.

“The rhetoric will kind of take care of itself,” Kellogg said. “Look at what’s happening on the ground.”

That’s all in exchange for an effort to bring down global diesel prices that have remained stubbornly high, mostly because of the Iran war, which has throttled traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Russia’s conflict with Ukraine also played a role, after Russia extended a ban on diesel exports through September following a wave of Ukrainian drone strikes on the country’s refineries.

Unfortunately for Trump, even if Russian diesel reaches the global market in the coming weeks, it probably won’t offer much relief for American farmers and truckers before the midterms.

The first release of 2.25 million barrels in October is 1.4 million barrels less than American consumers used in a single day as of early in the month. Shipments from Russia to the East Coast typically take more than two weeks, and record-high shipping costs would also likely push prices higher.

If Russian refineries are able to resume some exports, it would provide marginal relief to a global oil market that’s sorely missed the supply, analysts say. Yet whether those shipments restart in earnest depends on the durability of an energy ceasefire that Trump announced over the weekend. Neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to such a deal.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said monthly diesel exports of three million tons — near levels seen before Ukraine’s drone campaign — will only be possible after December.

“There is no indication that any diesel is making its way to the US just yet,” Bloomberg geoeconomics analyst Alex Kokcharov wrote in a note. “Given questions around the legality of easing sanctions and Russia’s own export capacity, it’s not clear this will result in any net increase to global diesel supplies.”

title: Thailand eyes US$30 departure tax for tourists in revenue push
article:
(Oct 13): Thailand is looking to travellers for more revenue, testing a tourism industry that has yet to fully recover from the pandemic.

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul’s government is considering an outbound tax of about 1,000 baht (US$30 or $38) on Thai and foreign travellers leaving the country, while separately planning a 450-baht fee for foreign visitors arriving by air.

The measures highlight a difficult trade-off for an economy already struggling with subdued domestic demand and sluggish growth. Thailand needs to raise more revenue after years of budget deficits of about 3%-4% of gross domestic product have eroded its fiscal space. But tourism is a major source of jobs, spending and foreign-currency earnings.

The Thai Travel Agents Association warned the outbound tax could sharply reduce passenger numbers, prompting airlines to cut flight frequencies and ultimately hurting inbound tourism. Such an outcome would also run counter to the government’s ambition to turn Thailand into a regional aviation hub, the group said.

Thailand welcomed about 24 million foreign tourists through Oct 10, down 4% from a year earlier and still well below the nearly 40 million recorded in 2019 before the pandemic. The Tourism Authority of Thailand expects about 33 million visitors this year. A total below last year’s 32.97 million would mark the first back-to-back annual decline outside the pandemic since at least 1995.

The proposed departure tax would revive a levy last set at 500 baht about two decades ago, said Finance Ministry Permanent Secretary Lavaron Sangsnit. Existing law allows the government to charge as much as 5,000 baht, though Lavaron said the rate under consideration is around 1,000 baht.

See also: American Airlines to expand Starlink WiFi across entire fleet

The tax could be incorporated into airline tickets rather than collected separately at departure, Lavaron said. He argued that people who can afford to travel overseas have greater ability to bear the additional cost, with proceeds potentially used to promote domestic tourism and fund travel insurance or emergency medical coverage.

The government also plans to charge foreign visitors arriving by air 450 baht, according to Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul. More than 80% of respondents supported the proposal in a recent online public consultation, he said.

title: Marco Polo Marine CEO’s father increases stake in company
article:
Shares of Marco Polo Marine (MPM) have seen weakness in recent weeks, dipping below 12 cents on some days.

Presumably seeing an opportunity to scoop up shares on the cheap, Lee Wan Teng, the founder of MPM and father of current CEO Sean Lee, has purchased 1.7 million shares for $202,045, or at an average price of 11.885 cents per share, from the open market.

This raises the elder Lee’s direct and deemed interest in MPM to 13.49%, up from the previous 13.45%.

For 3QFY2026 ended June 30, MPM reported y-o-y revenue growth of 13% to $35.7 million, lifting 9MFY2026 revenue by 30% y-o-y to $109.7 million. Gross profit for the quarter and nine months respectively was up 7% y-o-y to $15 million and 30% y-o-y to $46.4 million.

The company is in the process of several corporate actions. On Sept 7, Fuji Offset Plates Manufacturing moved ahead with the planned $139 million reverse takeover deal of MPM’'s shipyard business.

Offshore wind company PKR Offshore, in which MPM owns a 49% stake, had also planned to submit its application for a listing on the Taiwanese stock exchange during the third quarter. However, no announcement has been made as yet of the submission.

See also: Q&M’s Ng in married deal with IOI Properties’ non-independent non-executive director involving 14 mil shares

As at 10.13am on Oct 13, shares in Marco Polo Marine are flat at 12 cents.

title: DayOne inks multi-currency financing arrangement with seven banks
article:
Singapore-headquartered data centre operator DayOne has secured a multi-currency financing arrangement with a consortium of seven banks. Its members include: CIMB, Crédit Agricole CIB, DBS Group (DBS) (SGX:D05 ) , Maybank, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) (SGX:O39 ) , Standard Chartered and the United Overseas Bank (UOB) (SGX:U11 ) .

The financing arrangement comprises a US$2.4 billion ($3.1 billion) offshore term loan facility as well as a RM5.5 billion ($1.7 billion) Murabahah facility agreement, adding up to RM15 billion. A Murabahah facility agreement is an Islamic financing structure that does not charge interest. Instead, it is a cost-plus financing arrangement where the bank buys an asset on behalf of its client and sells it back to them with a markup.

With this new financing arrangement, DayOne’s total financing now stands at RM30 billion. This includes the RM15 billion of multi-currency financing it secured last year. The additional financing will help support the company’s continued development of its data centre operations in Johor, Malaysia.

On Oct 6, DayOne announced that it had filed for an IPO on the Nasdaq. Previously in May, Reuters, citing an unnamed source, reported that the company was considering a US$5 billion dual listing on the Nasdaq and Singapore Exchange (SGX).

title: Australia regulator halts another credit fund amid crackdown
article:
(Oct 13): Australia’s securities regulator temporarily barred Fidante Partners Ltd from offering units in a credit fund, extending a clampdown on private credit investments amid concerns over risks to investors.

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (Asic) issued a 21-day interim stop order against Class A units of the Ares Global Credit Income Fund, citing deficiencies in how the product’s target investors were identified. The regulator questioned whether the fund was suitable for investors seeking to preserve capital, as well as provisions allowing investors to allocate as much as 50% of their investable assets to the product.

The move comes just days after ASIC imposed interim stop orders on three mortgage investment funds operated by Australian Secure Capital Fund, which collectively manage about A$250 million (US$174 million). Those orders followed concerns over inadequate disclosures about loan portfolios and the costs investors could face when exiting the funds, underscoring growing regulatory scrutiny of an industry facing questions over transparency and liquidity risks.

“Where ASIC identifies concerns that products may be reaching retail investors they were not designed for, we will use our regulatory tools to act swiftly to intervene early, disrupt poor practices and protect investors from potential harm,” the regulator said in a statement on Tuesday.

Ares Global Credit Income Fund, which had A$799.9 million under management as of June 30, invests in global bonds, syndicated loans, asset-backed securities and collateralised loan obligations, according to Asic.

Asic said its latest intervention was part of broader surveillance of private credit funds, focusing on how products are distributed to retail investors, as well as fees, profit margins and potential conflicts of interest.

title: Goldman says markets underestimating how far yuan can rise
article:
(Oct 13): A stronger yuan is among the most underpriced scenarios in the world’s US$9.5 trillion ($12.2 trillion)-a-day foreign exchange market, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc’s Kamakshya Trivedi.

China’s currency is undervalued by around 20% to 25%, an estimate the bank’s global head of foreign exchange, rates and emerging markets strategy research calls “conservative.” He added that the nation’s swelling trade surplus strengthens the case for appreciation.

Goldman sees the yuan strengthening to 6.40 per dollar from around 6.69 in a year’s time, with the firm’s fair-value metrics pointing to a six handle as a future possibility, Trivedi said in an interview last week. China’s currency last traded near 6 in early 2014 amid rapid hot money inflows.

“People underestimate how far this can move,” said Trivedi. “At every stage as we’ve shifted the forecast stronger, I think I’ve been surprised by the extent to which consensus and forward markets still haven’t caught up to that.”

“Our view is very simple: we think it will be a gradual process, but it’s going to be sustained,” he added.

Goldman’s view comes as China confronts growing criticism from major trading partners such as European nations that it is using an artificially weak currency to boost exports. Beijing has rejected such claims, arguing that exchange-rate adjustments won’t resolve structural imbalances in the global economy, while adding that China’s export strength stems from its rising industrial competitiveness.

See also: South Korean won hits two-year high on lower oil, dollar sales

International pressure on the yuan has intensified even as Chinese authorities have allowed it to rise against most major peers, with the tightly managed currency appreciating to a four-year high versus the dollar. The yuan’s strength makes it one of the few currencies positioned for more sustained appreciation at a time when the greenback has rebounded due to geopolitical tensions and stubborn inflation.

Trivedi said the magnitude of the yuan’s undervaluation would look “much bigger” when factoring in China’s current account and external balance performance. China’s trade surplus stood at US$805.5 billion for the first eight months of the year, official data showed.

“So to my mind, there is no question that currency is significantly undervalued,” he said.

See also: Yuan hits four-year high versus basket as PBOC backs FX policy

Trivedi said Chinese policymakers may be becoming more comfortable with further yuan appreciation, partly due to the importance of stable trade relations.

China staved off wider trade frictions with the European Union by agreeing to curb exports of hybrid vehicles following talks that ended Friday. The yuan has appreciated more than 8% against the euro this year.

Beijing’s growing ease with a stronger currency also reflects the changing nature of the country’s export machine that is increasingly powered by cutting-edge technologies and advanced manufacturing.

“If you think about it even from China’s perspective, I think what is most important to them is the stability of trading relationships,” he said. “The longer you get stability in the trading relationships, I think they recognise that some degree of appreciation in the currency is consistent with the underlying macro.”

“China’s growing role as a provider of global funding marks a new phase of yuan internationalisation, extending the currency’s reach beyond trade settlement and payments into global borrowing, investment and hedging markets,” said Bloomberg strategists.

Trivedi also sees a stronger yuan aligning with Beijing’s goal of boosting the currency’s global role. Chinese President Xi Jinping had previously pledged to build a powerful currency that is widely used in international trade, investment and foreign exchange markets, holding the status of a global reserve currency.

“Modest, gradual but sustained appreciation I think serves that purpose of internationalisation as well,” Trivedi said. “It makes the return picture in Chinese assets a bit more attractive.”

title: Singapore bank sell-off tests city-state’s safe haven status
article:
(Oct 13): A sell-off in Singapore bank shares driven by fears of earnings downgrades is threatening one of Asia’s best-performing major stock benchmarks this year, putting the city-state’s safe haven status to the test.

The Straits Times Index has slid 6.6% from its peak more than five weeks ago, dragged lower by DBS Group Holdings Ltd, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and United Overseas Bank Ltd. The lenders account for more than half of the benchmark and shed a combined US$22.4 billion ($28.7 billion) in market value last week alone.

The sell-off reflects growing concern that local banks are entering a tougher phase ahead. Elevated bond yields are eroding the appeal of their dividend payouts, while the lenders will also have to account for losses on their holdings. That’s prompted Wall Street brokers to warn of downside risks to earnings released next month.

“The risk is a longer sell-off that spreads beyond the banks, or earnings and capital returns that start to weaken,” said Alex Ho, a sales trader at CMC Markets Singapore. “November’s results will be the first real test.”

Prior to the recent slump, Singapore stocks had hit a string of highs as earnings growth and market stability attracted institutional investors seeking shelter from gyrations tied to the escalating Iran war and AI trade. Investors are now backing away, with analysts increasingly wary about expectations remaining too optimistic into year end.

See also: Singapore power rates to fall from record after fuel price drop

JPMorgan Chase & Co warned on Wednesday that rising long bond yields will result in high mark-to-market losses on banks’ trading books and hurt capital activity for Southeast Asian banks. Separately, Citigroup Inc downgraded OCBC to ‘sell’ and iterated its ‘sell’ on UOB last week. HSBC Holdings Plc has also cut Singapore stocks to ‘neutral’ as valuations become stretched and financial conditions weigh on the real estate sector.

The strong rally in Singapore banks earlier this year has made the sector an outlier when compared with regional and global peers on a valuation perspective. Even after the recent pullback, DBS — the country’s largest lender — trades at 16.9 times its 12-month forward earnings compared with 13.2 times for MSCI financials gauge.

Not everyone is turning cautious, though. Some strategists argue that Singapore’s growth prospects coupled with the government’s efforts to rejuvenate the equities market should limit downside risks, even if the jury is out on the moves in the shorter term.

See also: You don’t need deep pockets to survive in F&B

“Critically, there are still no overtly concerning signs of bad debt, which tend to characterize bear markets for the banks, while loan growth is relatively healthy,” according to Jen-Ai Chua, Asia equity research analyst at Julius Baer. “As we enter the traditionally turbulent month of October, the only thing we can be sure of is more volatility in price action ahead,” she said.

article:

title: Jardine Matheson raises underlying earnings guidance for FY2026; assumes full control of Gammon Construction
article:
Jardine Matheson has raised its FY2026 earnings guidance to reflect "continued solid performance" across its portfolio.

From US$5.33 per share, Jardine Matheson now expects its underlying earnings per share to reach between US$5.50 and US$5.65. This metric is adjusted for disposals and reclassifications in the preceding FY2025.

Jardines Matheson will provide its regular interim update on Nov 20.

In addition, Jardine Matheson has completed the acquisition of a 50% stake in Gammon Construction previously held by its JV partner Balfour Beatty for US$330 million.

Jardines has been an investor in Gammon since 1969 and with full ownership of this entity, expects "modestly accretive" earnings from its first year.

Lincoln Pan, CEO of Jardine Matheson calls Gammon Construction the second "significant transaction" in 2026 and is a strategic, synergistic expansion of its Jardine Engineering & Infrastructure vertical.

See also: Amazon in talks to buy AI startup Decart, WSJ reports

"Our goal remains doubling the earnings of JE&I in the coming years by focusing on strategic investments that expand controlled earnings and capabilities across Asia," he adds.

Kevin O’Brien, CEO of Jardine Engineering & Infrastructure, calls Gammon Construction a "high-quality business with a strong reputation, deep customer relationships and talented people."

 

He sees significant opportunities for Gammon across the region, such as projects in Hong Kong's Northern Metropolis, as well as in Singapore and the wider region.

Jardine Matheson shares traded at $56.02 as at 9.09 am, up 0.344%.

title: Asian stocks to fall after US chipmaker sellof
article:
(Oct 13) : Asian stocks were set to decline as a selloff in chipmakers weighed on sentiment ahead of a pivotal earnings season and US inflation data that could shape the Federal Reserve’s next move.

Equity-index futures for Japan, Hong Kong and South Korea pointed lower, while those for Australia edged higher. US stock contracts were little changed after a gauge of chipmakers fell 2.7% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.7%. Treasury futures fluctuated ahead of the resumption of cash trading following a US holiday. A Bloomberg gauge of dollar strength climbed to its highest since mid-May 2025.

Micron Technology Inc. fell 3.9% and US-listed shares of SK Hynix Inc. dropped 4% after Chinese rival CXMT said it made progress on a memory-chip design capable of storing more data. Sandisk Corp. slid 6%, among the S&P 500’s biggest decliners.

Enthusiasm for artificial intelligence eased as investors weighed the outlook for capital spending against rising borrowing costs. Wall Street’s equity bull entered its fifth year, with the S&P 500 up nearly 120% from its 2022 low, putting the onus on earnings growth to justify elevated valuations.

“Growth has been powerful enough to keep valuations in check and allow investors to look past higher yields, interest rates and inflation,” said Bret Kenwell at eToro. “Another strong quarter could reinforce the bull narrative intact into year-end, while a disappointment could catalyze a broader pullback.”

US oil edged lower in early trading after Brent advanced 1.8% Monday as Ukraine cast doubt on an “energy ceasefire” touted by US President Donald Trump and Saudi Arabia faced fresh Houthi attacks following the deadliest strikes since the start of the Iran war.

See also: Oil holds advance as expanding Middle East war threatens supply

“We now expect Brent crude to average above US$100 a barrel through the second quarter of next year following attacks on Red Sea export infrastructure and a more persistent geopolitical risk premium,” Stephen Hare, lead economist at Oxford Economics, wrote in a note. “Prices decline thereafter as supply normalizes, but the return towards long-run equilibrium is now slower than previously expected.

The earnings season in the US gets underway Tuesday, with Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc. and Wells Fargo & Co. due to report. Bank of America Corp. and Morgan Stanley follow Wednesday. S&P 500 companies are estimated to post a 25% increase in third-quarter profits from a year earlier, according to data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence.

Investors will also be focusing on Wednesday’s consumer price index, likely the most important economic report the Fed will see before its October meeting.

See also: Bank stocks mired in correction into earnings as yields rise

Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said smaller, more frequent policy adjustments can help keep inflation expectations anchored, though she stopped short of backing another rate increase this month.

“This week’s CPI report is likely to be the most important release of data the Fed will see before its October meeting,” Jason Pride, chief of investment strategy and research at Glenmede, wrote. “Barring a stronger than expected inflation reading, the Fed is likely to take a patient approach to its next rate hike.”

title: Oil holds advance as expanding Middle East war threatens supply
article:
(Oct 13) : Oil held a gain as a widening conflict in the Middle East threatened to hamper a recovery in supply from the region, while there were also doubts over US President Donald Trump’s claims of an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine.

West Texas Intermediate traded near US$93 a barrel after rising 2.1% in the previous session, while Brent settled near US$107 on Monday. A barrage of drone and missile attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants on Saudi Arabia’s main airport has intensified pressure on Washington to step up its efforts in the conflict in Yemen.

Meanwhile, Ukraine will continue attacks against Russia as Moscow keeps targeting its energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Trump said there had been were violations of his “energy ceasefire” but urged his Ukrainian counterpart and Russian President Vladimir Putin to come together and end the war.

Brent remains more than 70% higher this year as the US war on Iran roils energy markets. The attacks on Saudi Arabia came shortly after Riyadh-led forces in Yemen launched a campaign to retake Houthi-held territory, while strikes on tankers in the critical Strait of Hormuz have escalated — leading a growing number of vessels to turn away from a port in the United Arab Emirates that has been key in helping Persian Gulf oil exports recover to near prewar levels.

“Its been a dizzying few days of headlines,” said Scott Shelton, an energy specialist at TP ICAP Group, pointing to issues including Trump’s claims of an “energy ceasefire” as well as the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. “We are off to a messy start this week.”

title: Bank stocks mired in correction into earnings as yields rise
article:
(Oct 13) : Big US bank stocks are teetering in correction territory as the group kicks off earnings Tuesday, heightening the focus on executives’ outlook for the American consumer with long-term borrowing costs the highest in decades.

Wall Street’s largest banks are expected to unveil a quarterly stock-trading haul of nearly US$19 billion, according to analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg. Meanwhile, lending is seen increasing year-over-year and credit quality is likely to hold steady, analysts expect.

Even so, the benchmark KBW Bank Index has dropped around 12% since a mid-August peak, exceeding the 10% threshold for a technical correction. The slump has coincided with a surge in Treasury yields and the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate hike in three years. The bank gauge is coming off its worst quarter since early 2023, when a prior episode of rising yields helped trigger a regional bank crisis that hit shares.

Banks, which need to balance how much they pay out for deposits with what they earn on loans, have been stung by the bond volatility, and they’re also under pressure as rates on credit-card, auto and home loans are climbing, says Matt Miskin at Manulife John Hancock Investments.

Lenders can benefit as “higher yields can lead to better revenues, but they can also lead to a tipping point where consumers just can’t pay these kinds of loans,” said Miskin, a strategist.

Reports from the banking giants start rolling in before the market opens on Tuesday, with announcements from Citigroup Inc., Goldman Sachs Group Inc., JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Wells Fargo & Co. On Wednesday, Bank of America Corp. and Morgan Stanley report.

See also: US stocks waver on slowest trading day in 2026

Last month, early reporter Jefferies Financial Group Inc. said its investment bank and equity-trading desk had a record quarter, though other metrics were mixed.

Options traders were leaning bullish on JPMorgan, the largest US bank, before the results, trading at the end of last week showed. Demand for upside calls that pay out on a 10% move outweighed the appetite for insurance against a 10% drop. Plus, there were more calls outstanding than puts, a potentially bullish signal.

So far, the economy is proving resilient in the face of higher borrowing costs and elevated energy prices, which have fanned inflation concerns. Investors in bank shares have other worries, such as risks posed by artificial-intelligence agents and the potential fallout from the November midterm elections, with polls showing Republicans losing ground amid voter anger over the economy and the war in Iran.

See also: Oil rises on Mideast attacks, dollar edges high

Republicans tend to favor lighter oversight of the financial sector, leading JPMorgan analysts to predict that a surprise sweep by the party could favor lenders such as Bank of America, Citigroup and Wells Fargo.

Wells Fargo’s Mike Mayo is among the analysts with a more bullish take on bank shares. He said last month that the elections can “put a dent in de-regulation but should not derail it.” He was also optimistic the AI “scare trade” would reverse when banks release results as “trust at banks is a moat for deposits.”

And at Morgan Stanley, analyst Manan Gosalia called the selloff lately “an attractive entry point,” and recommended investors use it to position for a stronger 2027.

The analyst pointed to AI-related investing and an overall sturdy economy as supporting bank shares. As for rising interest rates, while that does raise banks’ cost of funding, “at the same time revenue should also move higher,” Gosalia said.

As for the coming days, CIBC Capital Markets strategist Christopher Harvey anticipates executives will express more caution about consumer health and the economy than they did a few months ago.

Nonetheless, the sector may be headed for a “relief rally,” he wrote in a Monday note. Banks have typically bounced after earnings when they’ve been lagging going into the announcements, he said.

And if that does happen, “we would use the pop as an opportunity to reduce exposure” given the macro headwinds the firms are facing. He prefers communication services and utilities sectors over financial stocks.

title: US stocks waver on slowest trading day in 2026
article:
(Oct 13) : A selloff in chipmakers left stocks wavering ahead of the earnings season, with traders also gearing up for this week’s inflation data that will be key in shaping the Federal Reserve outlook.

The group of chip giants posted its longest retreat since July, weighing on the S&P 500 despite gains in most of its firms. While trading volume in US equities was the lowest in 2026, the stock benchmark remained near a record as bets on solid corporate results defied elevated oil prices and bond yields. Treasury futures fluctuated, with the cash market closed for Columbus Day.

Wall Street’s equity bull run completed its fourth anniversary, with the S&P 500 up nearly 120% from the 2022 bottom. And investors are bracing for high-stakes corporate results that will be crucial to sustaining the rally. Profit resilience helps explain why stocks have remained so strong, said Bret Kenwell at eToro.

“Growth has been powerful enough to keep valuations in check and allow investors to look past higher yields, interest rates and inflation,” he added. “Another strong quarter could reinforce the bull narrative intact into year-end, while a disappointment could catalyze a broader pullback.”

While this week’s inflation data could be a near-term volatility trigger, the new earnings season may play a bigger role in shaping the market’s momentum into year-end, according to Chris Larkin at E*Trade from Morgan Stanley.

“Earnings growth remains supportive for equities and the recent valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into the third-quarter earnings season,” said Goldman Sachs Group Inc. strategists led by Christian Mueller-Glissmann. They raised their three-month view on stocks to overweight.

See also: Oil rises on Mideast attacks, dollar edges high

The earnings season gets underway Tuesday, when Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc. and Wells Fargo & Co. report results. Bank of America Corp. and Morgan Stanley’s figures are due on the following day.

S&P 500 firms are estimated to post a 25% jump in third-quarter profits compared with a year earlier, data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence show.

Meantime, Wednesday’s consumer price index is likely to be the most-important data the Fed will see before its October meeting, according to Glenmede’s Jason Pride and Michael Reynolds. Barring a stronger-than-expected report, the central bank will probably take a patient approach to its next rate hike, they added.

See also: Bond selloff may mean fewer rate hikes from global central banks

Fed Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said smaller, more frequent adjustments to policy can help inflation expectations remain anchored, but she stopped short of backing a rate increase this month.

title: S&P 500 hovers near all-time high before earnings
article:

Most companies in the S&P 500 rose despite renewed losses in chipmakers. With Corporate America navigating one of the strongest profit cycles in recent history, equities have also defied concerns about elevated energy costs and bond yields. Brent crude climbed to around US$107 a barrel. Treasury futures were little changed, with the cash market closed for Columbus Day.

The stock bull run is completing its fourth anniversary, with the S&P 500 surging nearly 120% from its 2022 bottom. And investors are gearing up for a high-stakes earnings season that will be crucial to sustaining that rally. Profit resilience helps explain why stocks have remained so strong, said Bret Kenwell at eToro.

“Growth has been powerful enough to keep valuations in check and allow investors to look past higher yields, interest rates, and inflation,” he added. “Another strong quarter could reinforce the bull narrative intact into year-end, while a disappointment could catalyze a broader pullback.”

The market may be susceptible to negative surprises, but the fact that it has continued to reach new highs amid challenges highlights the strength of longer-term artificial-intelligence tailwinds, said Chris Larkin at E*Trade from Morgan Stanley.

See also: Goldman strategists upgrade global stocks on earnings boost

“Earnings growth remains supportive for equities and the recent valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into the third-quarter earnings season,” said Goldman Sachs Group Inc strategists led by Christian Mueller-Glissmann. They raised their three-month view on stocks to overweight.

S&P 500 firms are estimated to post a 25% jump in third-quarter profits compared with a year earlier, according to data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence.

The earnings season gets underway on Tuesday, when Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Citigroup Inc and Wells Fargo & Co report results. Bank of America Corp and Morgan Stanley’s figures are due on the following day.

“The big banks tend to set the stage for the rest of earnings season largely since their performance reveals how the underlying economy is doing, and a strong economy is the key to a healthy earnings season,” said Clark Bellin at Bellwether Wealth.

title: LVMH sales at key unit fall as China woes hurt Louis Vuitton
article:
(Oct 12): LVMH’s biggest division posted a slump in sales last quarter as its key Louis Vuitton brand suffered from a boycott in China.

Organic revenue at the fashion and leather goods unit slid 5% in the third quarter, LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE said in a statement on Monday. Analysts were expecting a drop of 1.57%.

The division was “affected in the third quarter by the slowdown in demand in China,” LVMH said.

Louis Vuitton sales suffered in July and August in China after the brand won a trademark dispute against Molly Tea, a local tea maker, Bloomberg reported last month. The victory drew a backlash from Chinese consumers there who deemed it unfair of the world’s largest luxury group to take the much smaller company to court.

LVMH shares have fallen by more than 40% this year, putting them on track for the worst annual performance since the global financial crisis in 2008. While much of the industry is feeling the effects of the downturn in demand, LVMH’s stock is the worst performer this year among major luxury groups, followed by rival Hermes International SCA.

Hopes for a rebound in the wider luxury industry this year have been undermined by sluggish Chinese demand, the prolonged conflict in the Middle East and weaker consumer confidence.
